standard_prerequisites.name: Rankin-Cohen bracket formula for L
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof recalls the bracket expression (A.2) for the operator L from subsection 2.2 and rewrites its coefficients as rational functions of t.

standard_prerequisites.name: Basis of M_{2k}
standard_prerequisites.use: The expansion system of f at c0 is organised with the monomial basis of Lemma A.2.

core_obligations: Identification of t'/f (lines 727-738): t'/f is a meromorphic modular function, hence rational in t; its zeros and poles pin it to kappa^{-1}P(t), and the first q-coefficient fixes kappa=(-1)^n prod alpha_j.
First bracket (lines 740-748): compute [f,t'] explicitly and divide by 2ft'^2 to get the first-order coefficient P'(t)/P(t) as in (A.1).

Second bracket (lines 749-777): expand f at c0 via the Lemma A.2 basis, compute [f,f]_2=f^2 h_4 with h_4's leading term, derive hat rho_{n-3}=-3kappa^{-2}(n-2)^2 and kappa=-cs^{n-2}, and conclude the claimed form of -[f,f]_2/(12f^2t'^2) with rho_i=-hat rho_i kappa^2/12.
proof_roadmap: Prove the identity (-1)^n (prod alpha_j) t' = f P(t) with the exact constant.
Compute the Rankin-Cohen bracket [f,t'] and read off the P'/P coefficient.
Expand f at the cusp, compute [f,f]_2, and normalise the constant term to get rho_{n-3}=(n/2-1)^2 and the remaining rho_i.

standard_prerequisites.use: The proof normalises the comparison Hauptmodul 'as in Lemma 3.1' before comparing q-expansions at infinity.

core_obligations: Zero property (line 479): rho_F is a zero of E_{alpha,j} for j=0,1,2 by construction of the Fuchsian value.
Converse setup (lines 481-482): take rho_1 with the identity holding for all j; univalence of t_{alpha,rho1} makes it a Hauptmodul for Gamma(rho1); the point is to show Gamma(rho1)=Gamma(rho_F).

Normalisation and expansion (lines 484-494): normalise the map as in Lemma 3.1, expand a^{-1}t at infinity from the basis of solutions of the uniformising equation of X_{ab} as in subsection 4.1, and compare with the power series built from the basis for accessory parameter rho_1.

Identification (lines 495-498): comparing the two series shows the solution ratios differ by a constant factor, so hat y_{alpha,rho1}/y_{alpha,rho1} induces a biholomorphism, i.e. rho_1 is the Fuchsian parameter; uniqueness gives rho_1=rho_F.
proof_roadmap: State the forward zero property of rho_F.
Assume rho_1 satisfies the system; show t_{alpha,rho1} is a Hauptmodul of Gamma(rho1).
Normalise as in Lemma 3.1 and compare the two q-expansions at infinity.
Conclude the solution-ratio comparison forces rho_1=rho_F by uniqueness of the Fuchsian parameter.

standard_prerequisites.name: Automorphisms of the four-punctured sphere
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same unit source (verbatim spans of doi:10.3842/SIGMA.2022.024), section 3 discussion before Lemma 3.1
standard_prerequisites.use: The existence of an automorphism mapping the cusp infinity to the puncture 0 is invoked and the author points to the next section; the normalisation argument only composes with it and conjugates by a diagonal sigma.

core_obligations: Existence (lines 176-179): start from any uniformising pair and compose the Hauptmodul with an automorphism so that the cusp infinity maps to the puncture 0.
Conjugation (lines 180-185): for real nonzero a,b conjugate by sigma=diag(a,1/a) and transport t; the generator of the stabiliser of infinity depends only on a, so choose a to force it to be T.
Cusp value (lines 186-189): t(0)=t_1(b); pick b real with t_1(b)=alpha^{-1}; the resulting (Gamma_alpha, t) is the desired normalised pair and is unique.
proof_roadmap: Compose the given Hauptmodul with an automorphism of X_alpha to send infinity to 0.
Conjugate the group by a diagonal sigma and read off how the stabiliser generator depends on a; fix a.
Fix b so that the normalised Hauptmodul takes the value alpha^{-1} at 0.
